messages:
alice_kim: Quick sync — we need to finalize the Dedicated -> Hosted handshake for routing. Two questions: (1) when is Hosted allowed to accept traffic from a Dedicated tenant, and (2) what telemetry/console surfaces do we need to make this visible to customers and SREs?

raj_patel: Short answer: honor contract first. If customer opted into Dedicated isolation, NO overflow to Hosted. For non-isolated tenants, we should prefer Dedicated, but allow an automatic overflow when Dedicated latency or throughput degrades beyond SLO.

maria_lopez: +1 to honoring isolation flag. For the non-isolated case we need a clear priority matrix: region affinity -> customer tier -> model variant compatibility -> cost preference.

sam_w: For model variants, fallback should only go to compatible variants (same tokenizer/opt semantics). Otherwise we risk output mismatch. We should encode compatibility as a small fingerprint (arch, vocab_id, quantization-profile).

ops_bot: deploy: routing-policy-service v2 deployed to canary (svc/route-policy). Logs: route_policy: accept_handshake=true for canary tenants.

gretchen_h: UX ask: in Console, show a live "overflow events" stream per tenant + per-route metric for "fallback_rate" (count and pct). Pager if fallback_rate > 5% for >5m for premium customers.

eva_grant: Also surface cost delta — if fallback moves to a larger model or to hosted multi-tenant pool that increases token cost, customers should see projected spend impact and opt-out toggle.

raj_patel: Implementation idea: two options for the handshake: (A) proactive routing in the edge/proxy: it checks Dedicated capacity and routes directly to Hosted if local policy allows, or (B) Dedicated backend returns a reserved response code (X-REDWOOD-OVERFLOW) and edge rewrites and sends to Hosted. I prefer A for latency, B for auditability. Thoughts?

alice_kim: I prefer B. If Dedicated signals overflow explicitly we keep the decision and audit trail inside Dedicated's control plane. Also easier to add reasons (e.g., 'gpu OOM', 'queueing', 'maintenance').

sam_w: B requires a small protocol change: response header + body hint. Example:
```
HTTP/1.1 409 Conflict
X-Redwood-Routing-Action: overflow
X-Redwood-Overflow-Reason: queue_backpressure
X-Redwood-Allowed-Targets: hosted:us-east-1, hosted:eu-west-1
```
Edge will map that to a routing decision.

maria_lopez: We must ensure tokens/data don't leak across isolation boundaries. If a tenant is "private_dedicated" then we cannot serialize request payloads to Hosted. So B must be gated by tenant.allow_hosted_fallback.

gretchen_h: UX: in Rollouts view add a column "Routing Guardrails" that lists allow_hosted_fallback, allowed_regions, preferred_variant_set. That way SEs can see when a canary will talk to Hosted.

raj_patel: Telemetry tags we should add for every request: routing.origin_pool, routing.final_pool, routing.reason, routing.fallback_chain (short list), model.variant_id. That will let us compute fallback_rate and latency delta.

eva_grant: For billing: event "routing.fallback" should carry estimated token cost multiplier so billing can show an "estimated delta" before actually charging. Console should record each fallback event in a timeline for the customer.

sam_w: Edge case: what if Hosted accepts but with a cheaper, smaller variant because of cost preference? We need an explicit variant selection algorithm: prefer same-arch same-vocab, then prefer equal or smaller parameterization, unless customer has "prefer_quality_over_cost" flag.

alice_kim: Good point. Let's add route config fields:
```
route: {
  prefer_regions: ["us-east-1"],
  allow_hosted_fallback: true/false,
  fallback_policy: "prefer_compatible_variant|force_same_size|allow_smaller",
  sla_tier: "premium|standard|trial"
}
```
This will live in project config and be editable in Console.

maria_lopez: From a safety perspective, we also need a circuit-breaker that flips to Reject rather than fallback if fallback_rate is high system-wide — to avoid cascading to Hosted and thrashing. Circuit state should be visible in Console and emitted as alerts.

ops_bot: metric: routing.fallback_rate{tenant,region} reported. Circuit breaker state: cb.routing.overload{region}=open/closed.

raj_patel: On API shape: internal debate — should we return a structured error with hint or a machine-readable status? I vote structured JSON error with fields {code, reason, allowed_targets}. Edge can parse that deterministically.

sam_w: Agreed. Keep the HTTP status distinct (409/503) but include the structured body. Prevents brittle header parsing.

eva_grant: For audits and security reviews: dedicated tenants flagged as "no_fallback" must appear in a compliance report. Also we need an admin override path for emergency operator action.

gretchen_h: UX for that admin override: in Console -> Tenant -> Actions -> "enable-hosted-rollout (temp)" with an internal change log + required justification. Show duration and auto-revert.

alice_kim: Next steps: (1) Raj to spec protocol body and error shape, (2) Sam to add fingerprinting for model compatibility, (3) Maria + Gretchen to design Console guardrails and alerts, (4) Eva to prototype billing delta events, (5) Ops to add telemetry tags. Can we sync tomorrow 11:15?

raj_patel: I'll drop an API PR with example error body.

maria_lopez: I'll sketch the guardrails mock and link to Figma.

sam_w: I'll add compatibility fingerprint RFC to docs.

eva_grant: I'll add a billing event schema.

alice_kim: Thanks — if anyone objects to the "no overflow for isolated tenants" rule speak now. Otherwise I'll lock that into the policy doc and start a short RFC. :thumbsup:

raj_patel: no objections from me.

maria_lopez: none from me.

sam_w: none.

eva_grant: none.

gretchen_h: none.

ops_bot: note: thread archived after 7 days of inactivity
